draft.title: How new evidence changes science
card: Scientific ideas are based on the evidence we have at the time. They can be explained, tested and checked by others.
New evidence can show that an idea is incomplete or wrong. Scientists may then change the idea so that it fits all the evidence.
New tools can produce new evidence. Better microscopes let people see living things that were too small to see before, such as bacteria.
A change in a scientific idea does not mean science failed. It shows that science responds to evidence.
draft.remember: When new evidence or tools appear, scientists can change an idea to fit it.

a.q: Why might a scientific idea about living things change?
opts: New evidence shows the old idea does not fit
A new scientist has taken over the research
The old idea has been around for a long time
Most people have stopped liking the old idea
a.why: Scientific ideas are judged against evidence, so evidence that does not fit an idea can lead to a change. Age or popularity does not decide whether an idea is kept.
a.clue: Think about what scientific ideas are based on.

b.q: In a town, Aiden uses a simple microscope and sees no living things in pond water. Years later, Priya uses a stronger microscope on the same water and sees tiny organisms moving. What does this show?
opts: A better tool can give new evidence that changes ideas
The pond water has changed into a different liquid
Aiden's microscope was better than Priya's microscope
Scientists should ignore results from new tools
b.why: The stronger microscope let Priya see organisms that Aiden's tool could not show. This new evidence can change what scientists think lives in pond water. Aiden's tool was not better, because it showed less.

a.best: New evidence shows the old idea does not fit

b.best: A better tool can give new evidence that changes ideas

problems.detail: The scenario says Priya looks 'years later' at 'the same water'. A student could fairly wonder whether the pond itself changed over those years, which weakens the conclusion that the tool made the difference. Have both people look at the same sample, or have Priya look soon after.

The right option stands out. It is the only one with the hedge 'can', and the only one using the card's key words 'tool' and 'evidence'. The distractors are plainly absurd, so a student could pick it without understanding the idea.
